_comment: L0 — the index a model selects from. See docs/EFFECT_CATALOGUE.md and. Entries are ONE PER TRIGGER, because trigger is the only axis that changes the emitted program: effect and target are token substitutions, a trigger is a different scaffold. Measured over the vocabulary learned from 535 real mods, 7 triggers cover all 32 abilities and these 3 cover 23 of them. COMMAND carries a whole vanilla command, which is the one thing the agent already writes reliably — far less work than authoring CBScript, and it keeps effect × target out of the template entirely.

effects.who: anything that comes near and TARGET allows (default everything but players), except this creature
effects.summary: Anything that comes close to this creature gets a potion effect — poison, slowness, blindness, anything vanilla. This is the 'its bite poisons you' shape. NOTE: it triggers on CLOSENESS, not on the actual bite.

AMPLIFIER.doc: 0 is level I, 1 is level II

TARGET.doc: WHO it lands on: mobs (the DEFAULT -- everything but players), monsters (only hostile mobs: zombies, skeletons, creepers...), animals, players (the child), everyone, or one creature like zombies or cows. Never the child unless the wish says so: 'its bite poisons YOU' / 'breathes frost at ME' / 'launch me' -> players (or everyone, if it is meant for anybody nearby); 'breathes fire at the monsters' -> monsters; 'poison the cow' -> cows. Leave it out and the child is never caught.

the spider bite should make you all slow and dizzy
i want the spider bite to make you slow for 10 seconds
effects.child_when: It happens the WHOLE TIME you are close to ${TAG}.

effects.who: other creatures carrying the ally tag

ALLY_TAG.doc: the tag its friends carry, e.g. soldier

AMPLIFIER.doc: 0 is level I, 1 is level II

effects.who: whoever just got hurt nearby and TARGET allows (default everything but players)
effects.when: when something takes damage near this creature
effects.summary: Runs your command the moment something is hurt next to this creature — the real 'its BITE does something' shape, and it works when the victim is ANOTHER MOB, not just the child. Write @s in your command to mean whoever was hurt. Approximate: anything damaged within RADIUS counts, so a hit from something else standing nearby also fires it. IT DOES NOT NEED YOUR CREATURE TO LAND THE HIT — it keys on the VICTIM being hurt nearby, never on who hurt it, so it still fires for a creature that never attacks anything (an agent talked itself out of on_hit believing a summoned giant might never attack, and fell back to proximity; measured, it fires even with the creature's AI switched off entirely).

TAG.doc: the creature's tag, e.g. spider — the same id you sculpted

COMMAND.doc: ONE vanilla command to run, with @s meaning WHOEVER JUST GOT HURT, e.g. 'effect give @s minecraft:slowness 10 1' or 'damage @s 4 minecraft:magic'. Things children ask for that ARE one command, and were measurably never reached for — these are not new features, they already work: "make it BURN them" / "set them on fire" -> data modify entity @s Fire set value 100s, which SETS IT ALIGHT for 5 seconds and the fire does the hurting (damage @s 4 minecraft:on_fire only HURTS: nothing catches fire. A player cannot be set alight this way, so for him use damage); other kinds of hurt -> damage @s 4 minecraft:freeze (or magic / lightning_bolt — the damage TYPE is a parameter); a ROAR as part of an effect -> playsound minecraft:entity.wither.spawn hostile @a ~ ~ ~ (its own growl, hurt cry, death cry and footsteps are its sculpt_creature voice, never a command); "make it GROW when it fights" -> attribute @s minecraft:generic.scale base set 2; "make it teleport BEHIND me" -> tp @s ^ ^ ^-2 (relative to facing, so 'behind' needs no maths); "make it go invisible" -> effect give @s minecraft:invisibility 10 1; "make it knock the sword out of my hand" -> clear @s minecraft:diamond_sword 1 — say it that way to the child, because it REMOVES the item rather than stealing it, and promising a steal would be a promise the command does not keep.

RADIUS.doc: how close counts as 'this creature did it'

TARGET.doc: WHO it lands on: mobs (the DEFAULT -- everything but players), monsters (only hostile mobs: zombies, skeletons, creepers...), animals, players (the child), everyone, or one creature like zombies or cows. Never the child unless the wish says so: 'its bite poisons YOU' / 'breathes frost at ME' / 'launch me' -> players (or everyone, if it is meant for anybody nearby); 'breathes fire at the monsters' -> monsters; 'poison the cow' -> cows. Leave it out and the child is never caught.

effects.summary: Runs your command the moment this creature LANDS: a quake, a splash, a puff of dust where it comes down. The 'it shakes the ground when it lands' shape. Fires on the landing only, never while it just stands there, so it does nothing at all until it has been in the air. Write @s in your command to mean whoever is near where it lands. A dust puff and a thump play by themselves.

COMMAND.doc: ONE vanilla command, with @s ALREADY meaning each one near where it landed -- never write @e[...] here. Left out, the ground jolts them up: the 'ground shakes when it lands' wish as it is. Or e.g. 'damage @s 4' (it hurts them), 'effect give @s minecraft:slowness 5 1' (it stuns them).

Leave it out and the child is never caught.

SOUND.doc: the thump: any vanilla sound id

effects.who: whoever is near it as it walks and TARGET allows (default everything but players)
effects.when: every few blocks it WALKS along the ground; never while it stands still
effects.summary: Runs your command as it WALKS: every STRIDE blocks of ground it covers, at its feet. The 'it does something with every step' shape: thumps that hurt what it walks past, sparks under its feet, a squelch. It never fires while the creature stands still (so 'only when it walks' is true), and a teleport is not a step. Write @s in your command to mean whoever is near it. A puff and a footstep play by themselves. To LEAVE something behind as it walks (flowers, snow), use trail instead.

TAG.doc: the creature's tag, the same id you sculpted

COMMAND.doc: ONE vanilla command, with @s ALREADY meaning each one near it as it steps -- never write @e[...] here, TARGET says who. E.g. 'damage @s 2' (it tramples them), 'effect give @s minecraft:slowness 3 1', 'data modify entity @s Motion set value [0.0d,0.4d,0.0d]' (bumps them up and out of its way). Left out: steps you only see and hear -- big stompy feet with a SOUND.

RADIUS.doc: how close to its feet counts, in blocks past its own side (a big creature's reach starts at its flank, not its middle)

STRIDE.doc: how many blocks it walks between steps (1 = every block, 3 = big slow strides)

TARGET.doc: WHO it lands on: mobs (the DEFAULT -- everything but players), monsters (only hostile mobs: zombies, skeletons, creepers...), animals, players (the child), everyone, or one creature like zombies or cows. Never the child unless the wish says so: 'its bite poisons YOU' / 'breathes frost at ME' / 'launch me' -> players (or everyone, if it is meant for anybody nearby); 'breathes fire at the monsters' -> monsters; 'poison the cow' -> cows. Leave it out and the child is never caught.

PARTICLE.doc: a puff under its feet each step: minecraft:poof | minecraft:crit | minecraft:snowflake | minecraft:flame

SOUND.doc: the footstep: any vanilla sound id

effects.summary: Runs your command on a timer — every few seconds, forever. The 'big fire every 15-30 seconds' shape, and how roars, waves of minions and auras are built.

TAG.doc: the creature's tag, e.g. spider — the same id you sculpted

COMMAND.doc: ONE vanilla command to run when it fires, e.g. 'effect give @a[distance=..4] minecraft:poison 5 1' or 'damage @e[tag=enemy,distance=..6] 4 minecraft:magic'. Write the target selector straight into it — that is how any effect and any target are expressed without a new template. Things children ask for that ARE one command, and were measurably never reached for — these are not new features, they already work: "make it BURN them" / "set them on fire" -> data modify entity @s Fire set value 100s, which SETS IT ALIGHT for 5 seconds and the fire does the hurting (damage @s 4 minecraft:on_fire only HURTS: nothing catches fire. A player cannot be set alight this way, so for him use damage); other kinds of hurt -> damage @s 4 minecraft:freeze (or magic / lightning_bolt — the damage TYPE is a parameter); a ROAR as part of an effect -> playsound minecraft:entity.wither.spawn hostile @a ~ ~ ~ (its own growl, hurt cry, death cry and footsteps are its sculpt_creature voice, never a command); "make it GROW when it fights" -> attribute @s minecraft:generic.scale base set 2; "make it teleport BEHIND me" -> tp @s ^ ^ ^-2 (relative to facing, so 'behind' needs no maths); "make it go invisible" -> effect give @s minecraft:invisibility 10 1; "make it knock the sword out of my hand" -> clear @s minecraft:diamond_sword 1 — say it that way to the child, because it REMOVES the item rather than stealing it, and promising a steal would be a promise the command does not keep.

PERIOD_TICKS.doc: 20 ticks = 1 second, so 200 is every 10 seconds

effects.child_when: It happens the WHOLE TIME you are close to ${TAG}.

effects.who: whoever the trigger catches and TARGET allows (default everything but players)
effects.when: on the chosen trigger, then spread over RAMP_TICKS ticks
effects.summary: push, launch or PULL creatures around -- knock back, send flying, or suck in like a magnet. Spread over ticks so it reads as a hit, not a teleport.

TAG.doc: the creature doing the pushing, e.g. giant

TRIGGER.doc: REQUIRED, no default -- say which one, because guessing builds the wrong ability silently. Match the child's own words: on_hit = they say when it HITS/punches/bites/smashes something ('whack me so hard i go flying'); proximity = they name a DISTANCE or say near/close ('from 15 blocks away', 'when you get close', 'pulls everything to it'); periodic = they name a TIME or say every/keeps ('every 5 seconds', 'stomps every 10 seconds') -- use with EVERY_SECONDS. If the wish names BOTH a contact verb AND a time ('knocks everyone back every 5 seconds'), the TIME WINS -- periodic. If the wish genuinely does not say WHEN, choose on_hit: an always-on aura cannot be escaped and reads as the game being broken, while a hit that guessed wrong sits quietly and can be tested on purpose. AND DO NOT TALK YOURSELF OUT OF on_hit: it does NOT need the creature to attack, or even to be ABLE to attack. It fires on the VICTIM's own hurt state within RADIUS and never asks who dealt the damage, so it works when the child hits the creature, when another mob does, and when the creature has no AI at all -- measured with the AI switched off. A real wish was lost to this: the agent chose on_hit three times, decided a summoned giant might never swing, and switched to proximity so that something would happen.

DIRECTION.doc: away (knock back) | up (launch skyward) | down (drag under, e.g. sucked into deep water) | toward (pull in, like a magnet or black hole)

STRENGTH.doc: nudge | shove | launch | huge. WORDS, not numbers -- a child says 'so hard i go flying'

FEEL.doc: ramp (spread over ticks so you SEE it -- almost always right) | snap (one instant shove; only when the wish really means instantaneous)

TARGET.doc: WHO gets pushed -- WHO it lands on: mobs (the DEFAULT -- everything but players), monsters (only hostile mobs: zombies, skeletons, creepers...), animals, players (the child), everyone, or one creature like zombies or cows. Never the child unless the wish says so: 'its bite poisons YOU' / 'breathes frost at ME' / 'launch me' -> players (or everyone, if it is meant for anybody nearby); 'breathes fire at the monsters' -> monsters; 'poison the cow' -> cows. Leave it out and the child is never caught. 'my dragon should fling the CREEPERS' -> creepers.

EVERY_SECONDS.doc: only with TRIGGER=periodic: how often it goes off, e.g. 5 for 'every 5 seconds'.

SOFT_LANDING.doc: yes | no. Launching someone into the sky is lethal on the way DOWN; yes gives them slow falling so the fun part is not followed by a death screen. Default yes for up-launches.

wishes: i want the giant to WHACK me so hard i go flying
make the monster launch me way up in the SKY
my magnet robot should pull all the zombies to him
effects._derived_note: Filled by apply_effect from the friendly words above, never by the agent. Kept OUT of `params` on purpose: params is the surface the agent is offered, and offering it a raw selector or a Motion vector would undo the entire point of asking for direction and strength in words.

effects.summary: RECOLOUR AN ORDINARY MOB — make a vanilla mob SHIMMER THROUGH ITS OWN COLOURS for ever: a RAINBOW axolotl, a rainbow sheep, a colour-changing parrot. Use this INSTEAD of sculpting a new creature when the child names a vanilla mob plus a colour or 'rainbow': summon the real mob with a tag, then apply this to that tag. Works on: axolotl, sheep, shulker, parrot, rabbit, llama, trader_llama, horse, mooshroom, fox, frog, cat.
effects.who: the tagged mob itself — its own colour changes
effects.when: all the time: one colour step every EVERY_SECONDS
effects.child_when: ${TAG} keeps changing colour all by itself — just watch it!

TAG.doc: the mob to recolour (the tag you summoned it with)

MOB.doc: which vanilla mob it is, so the right colours are used: axolotl, sheep, shulker, parrot, rabbit, llama, trader_llama, horse, mooshroom, fox, frog, cat. Any other mob has no colours to step through.

EVERY_SECONDS.doc: how long each colour lasts. 1 is a gentle shimmer; 0.25 is a disco.

wishes: make my axolotl rainbow coloured
a sheep that changes colour all the time
a rainbow parrot

effects.summary: leave a TRAIL behind it as it walks — snow, flowers, a carpet of colour — that fades after a while. For 'leaves ice / flowers / rainbow hoofprints behind it'. It only fills air and only ever takes back its own block.
effects.who: the ground it walks over (only empty air above solid ground)
effects.when: as it moves: a mark every few steps, each fading after LASTS_SECONDS
effects.child_when: ${TAG} leaves a trail behind it as it walks, and the trail fades away after a while.

TAG.doc: the creature that leaves the trail

BLOCK.doc: what it leaves — a THIN thing it can walk over: minecraft:snow (frost, ice, snow) | minecraft:poppy, minecraft:dandelion, minecraft:cornflower (flowers) | minecraft:red_carpet … (colour) | minecraft:moss_carpet. A full block is refused: it would be put round the creature's own feet.

PARTICLE.doc: a small sparkle where each mark lands: minecraft:happy_villager | minecraft:snowflake | minecraft:cherry_leaves | minecraft:glow

LASTS_SECONDS.doc: how long each mark stays before it fades. It ALWAYS fades — a trail that stays turns his world into carpet.

MOST.doc: the most marks down at once

wishes: a frost wolf that leaves frost wherever it walks
a slug that leaves a line of daisies behind it
a pony that leaves coloured footprints

effects.summary: DROPS an item at its feet every so often, for him to pick up — honey, eggs, flowers. Stops while MOST of its drops lie unclaimed, so it never floods the world.
effects.who: nobody: an item appears where it stands
effects.when: every EVERY_SECONDS, while fewer than MOST of its drops are lying about
effects.child_when: ${TAG} drops something for you every so often — pick it up!

ITEM.doc: the item id it drops: minecraft:honey_bottle | minecraft:egg | minecraft:fire_charge (a 'fire egg') | minecraft:poppy | any item

SOUND.doc: the little noise when it drops one

MOST.doc: it stops while this many of its drops lie unclaimed

wishes: a hen that lays golden eggs for me
a sheep that drops a cookie now and then
a little dragon that leaves fire charges for me

_child_when_note: The sentence the CHILD is told, spoken at finish_building and derived from what was actually BUILT rather than from what the agent meant to build. Separate from `when`, which is judge-facing and names parameters (`every PERIOD_TICKS ticks`) a seven-year-old cannot read. Required on every entry: an ability nobody can be told how to trigger is an ability the child concludes is broken.
